intro: Five themes moving drug development this week — ranked, with a point of view and the sources behind them. Refreshed every Monday.

narratives.headline: KRAS is still the most crowded target in oncology — and the crowd is reaching pivotal stage
narratives.detail: Four modalities are now pressing on the same target across PDAC and NSCLC at once: allele-specific small molecules (zoldonrasib's G12D Phase 3 enrolling alongside daraxonrasib, sotorasib and adagrasib, with VS-7375 behind in Phase 2), J&J's $1B Firefly Bio KRAS-ADC platform, and the standing neoantigen-vaccine lane (autogene cevumeran, ELI-002). Per pancreatic cancer's Phase 3 graveyard, none of it is de-risked — every read this cycle is an entrant or a phase advance, not validated efficacy. The crowding is the story; ESMO in September is where the cluster gets tested.

narratives.headline: Oral SERDs have settled where they actually win — and it isn't 1L monotherapy
narratives.detail: Roche's three same-cycle giredestrant reads land the point the class has been circling: pionERA failed in 1L monotherapy versus letrozole (PFS HR 0.89), while adjuvant lidERA cleared its bar (IDFS HR 0.65) and the post-CDK4/6 everolimus combination hit (PFS HR 0.56). The class — elacestrant, camizestrant and imlunestrant included — is consolidating around adjuvant and combination positioning rather than the AI-displacement fight it keeps losing. It's the clearest in-period signal yet of where these drugs belong.

narratives.headline: CD19 antibodies just broke into frontline DLBCL
narratives.detail: Tafasitamab's frontMIND read is the first CD19 antibody to win in frontline DLBCL (PFS HR 0.75), arriving with a fresh epcoritamab OS cut versus immunochemotherapy and the standing mosunetuzumab-plus-pola benchmark (PFS HR 0.41). After several cycles of bispecific and CD-targeting dominance confined to relapsed/refractory disease, the frontline door is now open too. The entrant tail — sonrotoclax, tazemetostat, allo-NK CD19 — is still early.

narratives.headline: HER2+ metastatic breast turns into an ADC-vs-TKI contest
narratives.detail: A tucatinib-plus-trastuzumab-and-pertuzumab triplet cleared Phase 3 in HER2-positive metastatic breast (PFS HR 0.641; 24.9 vs 16.3 months), giving the setting a credible TKI-anchored alternative to the T-DXd ADC standard. HER2+ MBC is now an ADC-versus-TKI-combination fight rather than ADC-only — a useful counterweight in a year when nearly every other modality story bends toward ADCs.

narratives.headline: The ADC benefit-risk bar is quietly tightening even as the class proliferates
narratives.detail: The Zynlonta Phase 3 three-fold death-rate signal was flagged independently this cycle by both the breast review — read across T-DXd, Dato-DXd, sacituzumab and patritumab-DXd — and the AML/MDS feed framing the CD123-ADCs pivekimab and BL-M11D1. It's a class-wide scrutiny signal rather than a single-asset miss, and worth watching precisely because so much of the rest of the pipeline is leaning on the modality.
